title: Add Two Integers
corePattern: Math - Direct Arithmetic and Bit Manipulation
interviewTips: Ask if you are allowed to use the + operator or must implement addition manually with bitwise logic.
Trade-off: direct + is O(1) and optimal in practice, bitwise XOR-AND loop is O(log M) and shows understanding of how adders work but is slower.
Edge-case tip: verify negative numbers, zero, and 32-bit overflow behavior, especially Python infinite-precision ints vs fixed 32-bit int in C++ and Java.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Direct Addition with Plus Operator
approaches.intuition: Adding two integers is a primitive CPU operation, so just return num1 + num2 directly. This is the intended solution for this Easy problem.
approaches.theory: Integer addition in hardware is constant time for fixed-width types. The language runtime maps + to a single ADD instruction. No extra data structures or loops are needed, so time and space are both constant.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single arithmetic operation, independent of input values.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only uses a few integer variables, no extra allocation.

edgeCases: num1 = -100, num2 = 100 gives 0 with sign cancellation

approaches.name: Approach 2: Bitwise Addition without Plus
approaches.intuition: Simulate a binary adder: XOR gives sum without carry, AND shifted left gives carry. Repeat until carry becomes zero.
approaches.theory: For bits a,b: a ^ b is sum ignoring carry, (a & b) << 1 is carry. Replacing a with a ^ b and b with carry and iterating propagates carries like ripple-carry adder. Terminates in at most 32 iterations for 32-bit ints. In Python mask to 32 bits with 0xFFFFFFFF to emulate fixed-width two complement and convert back at end.

timeComplexity.explanation: At most number of bits iterations, up to 32 for 32-bit int, where M is max absolute value. Each iteration is O(1) bitwise ops.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two integer variables num1 and carry, no extra memory.

edgeCases: Negative carry chain: -1 + 1 loops until carry clears, returns 0
Zero: 0 + 0 returns immediately with no loop
Python needs mask or negative inputs loop forever due to infinite sign extension
